partial: Partitioning/archival, partition retention/hold policy and cold read routing need an archive destination/tablespace and retention horizon. No such decision was supplied; it was requested during this lane. The globally unique chat_post identity and its foreign keys also need a coordinated partition identity design.

Sequence allocation still holds the route/privacy fence through insertion. Releasing it or making allocation nontransactional changes the existing route, authorization and rollback contract; it needs a coordinated decision and changes outside the owned store scope. The measured native budgets pass; the contention report does not claim 1000 simultaneous sends meet 30ms.

The implemented cache uses a post-transaction generation fence and lazy exact rebuilds. Connected-reader outbox warming, partitioned drains, operations-view metrics and application/client batch wiring are outside the owned files and are not implemented here.

The narrowed 2-million-post target is exercised. The planning target of 500 million posts, percentile series at 1/10/100/500 million, exact dead-tuple byte measurements and long-running autovacuum/concurrent live partition migration are not claimed. Browser, CI and race verification belong to the orchestrator.

new_findings: The client still makes one GetCounts request per room; the new batch store API is not wired into that loop.
The outbox receipt foreign key is on outbox_id alone; its tenant-leading primary key caused a full receipt scan for each retained parent deletion. Migration 00037 fixes this.

The pin query selected a parallel nested-loop plan at volume despite LIMIT 200. The equivalent correlated visibility lookup avoids that startup cost; both forms are measured in chatscale_pins_report_large.json.
Pool queuing dominates 1000 simultaneous send latencies even when individual send latency meets budget; the contention figures are evidence for the coordinated sequence/fence work.
